findings.observed: Financing that fits your plans / Competitive rates. Clear terms. No surprises.
findings.expected: Create and use a localized banner image (e.g. banner-fr.png) with French text: "Un financement adapté à vos projets / Taux compétitifs. Conditions claires. Aucune surprise."
findings.description: The hero banner on the French homepage displays an image containing hardcoded English text ("Financing that fits your plans", "Competitive rates. Clear terms. No surprises."). The image file is literally named banner-en.png and is reused unchanged on the French page.
The site footer copyright notice is left untranslated in English on the French version of every page (shared footer component).

On the French loan application form, submitting with an empty "Nom complet" field shows the validation message in English ("This field is required.") while every other field on the same form correctly shows the French message "Ce champ est obligatoire."

findings.observed: Merci. Votre demande pour {montant} a été reçue.
findings.expected: Merci. Votre demande pour 10 000,00 $ a été reçue.
findings.description: On the application confirmation page, the French confirmation message shows the raw template placeholder "{montant}" instead of the formatted loan amount. The English version correctly interpolates the amount.

The recent-transactions table on the French dashboard formats dates as US-style MM/DD/YYYY (e.g. "09/15/2026"), whereas the English version correctly uses ISO format (2026-09-15). This is both wrong for fr-CA convention and ambiguous/confusing (could be misread as day/month).
The "Recent transactions" section heading on the French dashboard is left untranslated in English, while the rest of the dashboard (e.g. the count span "3 opérations récentes") is translated.

findings.expected: Link should point to /fr/calculator when on the French dashboard.
findings.description: On the French dashboard, the "Estimer un nouveau prêt" link incorrectly points to /en/calculator, switching the user to the English version of the site instead of staying on /fr/calculator.

The "Pay later" checkbox label is mistranslated as "Payer maintenant" (Pay now), which is the opposite meaning. The help text below it ("Premier paiement reporté de 30 jours" / First payment deferred by 30 days) still matches the correct "pay later" behavior, confirming the label itself is wrong.

findings.observed: Aucune accusation pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.expected: Aucuns frais ne s'appliquent pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.description: "Accusation" is a false-cognate mistranslation of "charge" (fee); in French "accusation" means a criminal/legal accusation, not a monetary fee. It should be "frais".

findings.expected: Taux variable de 5,2 %, sous réserve d'approbation de crédit.
findings.description: The French rate disclaimer drops the qualifier "subject to credit approval" present in the English version, changing the meaning/completeness of the disclosure.

The estimated monthly payment amount on the French calculator page is displayed in US currency format ($450.91) instead of the Canadian French convention (450,91 $) used elsewhere on the site (e.g. dashboard balance "12 458,30 $").
The modal's "Close" button was translated as "Proche" (an adjective meaning "near/nearby"), instead of "Fermer" (the verb meaning "to close"). This is a false-cognate mistranslation.

findings.expected: Use a localized version of promo-a.png (matching "Variable rate: 5.2%") on the French page instead of promo-c.png, which shows unrelated content ("Taux fixe : 4,9 %").
findings.description: The French calculator page loads a different promo image (promo-c.png) than the English one (promo-a.png). The French image's visible text reads "Taux fixe : 4,9 %" (Fixed rate: 4.9%), which contradicts both its own alt attribute ("Taux variable : 5,2 %") and the surrounding page text about a 5.2% variable rate. This shows incorrect/contradictory information to French users.

The homepage subtitle uses the informal "tu" register ("Découvre tes options"), while the rest of the site (apply form, consent checkbox, error messages, calculator) consistently uses the formal "vous" register, e.g. "Vous devez donner votre accord avant de soumettre." This is an inconsistent register for a banking site.
